articles.title: Dharamshala Paragliding Horror: Gujarat Tourist Dies as Glider Collapses Mid-Air
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: #InShort | A tourist Satish (27) from Gujarat died in a horrific paragliding crash at Indru Nag on Monday (14 July 2025). Chilling video shows the glider collapsing seconds after takeoff. Authorities probe negligence as Kangra bans paragliding till Sept 15.

body.html:
#InShort | A tourist Satish (27) from Gujarat died in a horrific paragliding crash at Indru Nag on Monday (14 July 2025). Chilling video shows the glider collapsing seconds after takeoff. Authorities probe negligence as Kangra bans paragliding till Sept 15.

* * *

DHARAMSHALA — A 27-year-old tourist from Gujarat, Satish, died on Monday during a tandem paragliding flight at the Indru Nag site near Dharamshala, Himachal Pradesh. A chilling 10-second video shows ground staff pushing Satish and pilot Suraj off a slope before the glider collapsed seconds later.

Both were rushed to Zonal Hospital, then Satish was airlifted to Tanda Medical College, where he succumbed to injuries the same evening. Pilot Suraj is under treatment.

ASP Hitesh Lakhanpal said the SHO has been directed to investigate, and tourism officials will also examine if safety protocols were followed. Authorities are also checking if the site had proper technical clearance.

This is the second fatal crash at Indru Nag in six months. In January, 19-year-old Bhaveshawar Khushi from Gujarat also died here. Following Monday’s tragedy, Kangra DC Haimraj Bairwa banned paragliding across the district, including Bir-Billing, till September 15 citing monsoon risks.

Himachal has recorded over a dozen paragliding deaths in 30 months, often blamed on untrained or reckless pilots. Suresh Thakur of the Billing Paragliding Association slammed pilots for flouting rules yet facing no action.

Satish’s body will be handed over to his family after postmortem. Authorities are mulling suspension of the operator’s license for flying from a site reportedly not cleared by forest officials. The crash occurred just two days before the seasonal ban was set to begin.

articles.title: Filmy-Style Attack on Sarpanch in Broad Daylight Sparks Outrage in Surajgarh
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Surajgarh (Rajasthan) — Panic gripped Surajgarh town on Tuesday afternoon when unidentified miscreants attacked Kakoda village Sarpanch Sandeep Dalla in broad daylight near Barasiya College, leaving him and his companion Devi Singh Ola seriously injured.

body.html:
Surajgarh (Rajasthan) — Panic gripped Surajgarh town on Tuesday afternoon when unidentified miscreants attacked Kakoda village Sarpanch Sandeep Dalla in broad daylight near Barasiya College, leaving him and his companion Devi Singh Ola seriously injured.

According to eyewitnesses, around 10–12 attackers arrived in three camper vehicles, blocked the Sarpanch’s car on a busy road, and began attacking it with sticks and sharp weapons. The attackers smashed the vehicle and assaulted both occupants, terrifying onlookers and sending people running for cover.

Despite the brutal assault, Sandeep Dalla and Devi Singh Ola survived and were rushed to the hospital by police, who reached the spot soon after receiving information. The attack, executed in a filmy style, has created an atmosphere of fear and anger in the area, with locals calling it a complete failure of law and order.

Police suspect the attack may be linked to an old rivalry but are investigating all angles. CCTV footage from the vicinity is being examined to identify the attackers, and a forensic team has collected evidence from the scene. Raids are underway, and additional police force has been deployed to maintain peace.

The incident has triggered widespread outrage not just in Surajgarh but in nearby areas as well, with locals demanding immediate arrests and strict punishment for the culprits. The administration has assured that the accused will be caught soon and stern action will follow to prevent such incidents.

articles.title: Newly-Married HR Officer Crushed to Death by Speeding Container on Talegaon-Chakan Highway
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: #InShort | HR officer Gajanan Bolkekar (26), married just 3 months ago, was crushed to death by a speeding container on the Talegaon Chakan highway while heading to work. He fell from a bike & was run over. Residents blame potholes & reckless driving for repeated tragedies.

body.html:
#InShort | HR officer Gajanan Bolkekar (26), married just 3 months ago, was crushed to death by a speeding container on the Talegaon Chakan highway while heading to work. He fell from a bike & was run over. Residents blame potholes & reckless driving for repeated tragedies.

* * *

Pune, Maharashtra — In a heart-rending accident on the Talegaon-Chakan highway on Monday morning (14th), a 26-year-old human resource development officer was crushed to death under a speeding container while on his way to work.

The deceased has been identified as Gajanan Baburao Bolkekar, a resident of Bolka village, Kandhar taluka, Nanded district. He was employed as an HR at Panse Auto Com Unit in MIDC Chakan and had married just three months ago.

According to police, Gajanan was riding pillion with his colleague Aditya Gaikwad (23) on a two-wheeler, heading towards their company around 7:45 am. Near Hyundai Chowk in Khalumbe village limits, the container — allegedly driven recklessly by Mohammad Armaan Kamaruddin Khan (30), a resident of Dharavi, Mumbai — attempted to overtake them at high speed.

The two-wheeler skidded and Gajanan, seated at the back, fell under the rear wheels of the container and was crushed to death on the spot. Aditya Gaikwad sustained injuries in the crash.

The impact was so severe that Gajanan’s body was mangled, said officials. He had reportedly asked Aditya for a lift that morning as he was late for work.

Based on a complaint by eyewitness Vijay Shankarrao Tantarpale (24), Mhalunge MIDC police have booked Mohammad Khan for causing death by negligence.

Residents and commuters have blamed the hazardous conditions of the Talegaon-Chakan road — marked by potholes, congestion and reckless driving — for repeated fatal accidents.

Gajanan’s tragic and untimely death has left his family and colleagues shocked, with many mourning the loss of a young man who had just begun his married life.

articles.title: Stray Dogs Maul Indore Student on Exam Day — Alarming CCTV Footage Sparks Outrage
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: #InShort | A college student was mauled by a pack of stray dogs while walking to her exam in Shri Nagar Extension on July 12 2025.

body.html:
#InShort | A college student was mauled by a pack of stray dogs while walking to her exam in Shri Nagar Extension on July 12 2025.

* * *

INDORE — In yet another shocking case of stray dog menace, a college student was attacked and severely injured by a pack of dogs while heading for her exam in Indore’s Shri Nagar Extension area on Saturday morning, July 12.

The incident occurred around 6:30 AM when the student, accompanied by a friend, was walking to college. Four stray dogs suddenly charged at her, knocking her down and biting her legs. CCTV footage shows the young woman attempting to scare the dogs away but being overpowered as they returned in a pack and dragged her to the ground.

A friend riding a scooter spotted the attack and intervened just in time to drive the dogs away. The student, visibly shaken and bleeding, sat on the road in shock until nearby residents Vishal and Shaifali Agrawal rushed her to their home and cleaned her wounds. “She was on her way to the exam and had deep wounds on her leg. She was terrified,” the couple told local media.

The student later left with her friend for medical treatment.

Residents of the area blamed the growing stray dog population on the open dumping of leftover food from neighbouring Sonia Gandhi Nagar. “People dump non-vegetarian leftovers here every night despite regular garbage collection,” a resident said, calling the area a hotspot for dog attacks.

Local resident Anand Bagora said they have lodged multiple complaints through the Indore Municipal Corporation’s 311 app, after which garbage is cleared, but the problem persists and the dog population keeps increasing.

Data from Government-run Hukumchand Hospital shows over 24,000 dog bite cases reported in Indore between January 1 and July 13, 2025. While most victims recover after anti-rabies treatment, residents have demanded stricter action from the municipal corporation to control the menace and penalise those dumping food irresponsibly.

articles.title: Bulandshahr Shocker: Harassed by Wife and Her Lover, Man Ends Life
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Bulandshahr (UP) — A disturbing case of extreme mental and physical harassment has emerged from the Kakod police station area of Bulandshahr, where a 32-year-old man allegedly died by suicide after being tortured by his wife and her lover.

body.html:
Bulandshahr (UP) — A disturbing case of extreme mental and physical harassment has emerged from the Kakod police station area of Bulandshahr, where a 32-year-old man allegedly died by suicide after being tortured by his wife and her lover.

The deceased, identified as Asif, reportedly hanged himself at home on 11 July. According to his brother Abid, Asif had called him before taking the drastic step and described his ordeal in tears — alleging that his wife Rubina (28) and her lover Salim (25) tied his hands and feet, drugged him, and forced him to watch them have sexual relations “in porn film style” in front of him.

Asif and Rubina had been married for 10 years and had three children. Salim, the alleged lover, is a neighbour.

The family claims that Asif had even approached Rubina’s brother for help but was humiliated and told he was unworthy of his wife and should die. Unable to bear the constant humiliation and worried about his children, Asif ended his life.

Police have registered a case against Rubina and Salim on the complaint of Asif’s family. Both accused have been absconding since the incident. The body has been sent for post-mortem, and a search is underway for the duo.

The incident, which falls under the category of severe domestic violence and mental torture, has sparked outrage and raised serious questions about trust and dignity in relationships.

articles.title: Wife Pushes Husband Into Krishna River While Taking Selfie in Raichur; Locals Rescue Him
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Raichur (Karnataka) — A shocking incident was reported from Raichur district on Saturday, where a woman allegedly tried to kill her husband by pushing him into the Krishna River while taking a selfie.

body.html:
Raichur (Karnataka) — A shocking incident was reported from Raichur district on Saturday, where a woman allegedly tried to kill her husband by pushing him into the Krishna River while taking a selfie.

The husband, identified as Tatappa, managed to swim to a rock and cling to it, shouting for help. Locals heard his screams and rescued him using a rope. The incident occurred on a bridge over the Krishna River at Kadlur village, which borders Telangana’s Narayanpet district.

According to eyewitnesses, the wife asked Tatappa to take a selfie on the bridge. As they posed, she allegedly pushed him into the river. When villagers questioned him after the rescue, Tatappa told them, “I didn’t jump — my wife pushed me.”

A video of the rescue, now viral on social media, shows Tatappa holding onto a rope and being pulled ashore by 3–4 men.

While Tatappa claimed his wife intentionally pushed him due to ongoing marital disputes, the wife said it was an accident. The couple, who married in April 2025, have reportedly been in conflict since soon after their wedding.

Locals intervened, calmed them down, and called their parents. Both were eventually taken back home.

articles.title: Bareilly Teacher Faces Backlash Over Poem on Kanwar Yatra; Police Begin Probe
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Bareilly (UP) — A controversy erupted in Bareilly after a poem by Hindi lecturer and Swachh Bharat Mission brand ambassador Rajneesh Gangwar, recited during a school assembly, went viral on social media and drew protests from Hindu organisations.

body.html:
Bareilly (UP) — A controversy erupted in Bareilly after a poem by Hindi lecturer and Swachh Bharat Mission brand ambassador Rajneesh Gangwar, recited during a school assembly, went viral on social media and drew protests from Hindu organisations.

The poem, recited to children at MGM Inter College, questions the practice of carrying the Kanwar and instead urges students to pursue education and serve humanity. Among the lines that triggered outrage were:

"कांवड़ लेने मत जाना, तुम ज्ञान का दीप जलाना।
मानवता की सेवा करके, तुम सच्चे मानव बन जाना।"

In the viral video, Gangwar is seen addressing children and reading the poem, which also states:
"कांवड़ ढोकर कोई वकील, डीएम एसपी नहीं बना है।
कांवड़ जल से कोई बनिया, हाकिम, वैद्य नहीं बना है।"

Hindu organisations, including the Mahakal Seva Samiti and BJP leaders, alleged that the poem hurt the sentiments of Shiva devotees. On Saturday, BJP leader Rahul Gupta and Mahakal Seva Samiti president Shakti Gupta submitted a complaint at Baheri police station, demanding strict legal action. Several local leaders and devotees joined the protest, stating that such remarks could disturb communal harmony.

In his defence, Gangwar issued a statement on social media, clarifying that his intent was not to insult Sanatan Dharma or Kanwar Yatra, but to encourage students to attend school regularly, avoid crowds and addictions, and focus on education. He claimed his words were being misinterpreted and attributed the outrage to personal jealousy.

The police have registered a report based on the complaint and begun an investigation. The administration has yet to announce any formal action against the teacher.

This is the Poem: (translation might be inaccurate)

कांवड़ ढोकर कोई वकील, डीएम एसपी नहीं बना है।
No one has become a lawyer, DM or SP by carrying Kavad.

कावड़ जल से कोई बनिया, हाकिम, वैद्य नहीं बना है।
No one has become a merchant, ruler or doctor by carrying Kavad water.

कावड़ से बुद्धि-विवेक का तनिक विकास न होगा।
There will be no development of intellect and wisdom by Kavad.

भांग, धतूरा, गांजा, सुल्फा, मद से कोई उद्धार न होगा।
There will be no salvation from bhang, dhatura, ganja, sulpha and intoxication.

जाति-धर्म का नशा छोड़कर, स्वकल्याण करो तुम।
Leaving the addiction of caste and religion, do good for yourself.

शिक्षालय–पुस्तकालय में पढ़, ज्ञान प्रगाढ़ करो तुम।
Study in the school-library and deepen your knowledge.

सत्कर्मों से मानव सेवा कर, प्रेम का दीप जलाना।
Serve humanity with good deeds, light the lamp of love.

कावड़ लेने मत जाना, तुम ज्ञान का दीप जलाना।
Don't go to get Kavad, light the lamp of knowledge.

मानवता की सेवा करके, तुम सच्चे मानव बन जाना।।
By serving humanity, become a true human.

articles.title: Tourist's Car Plunges 300 Feet at Satara's 'Death Point' - One Critical, Four Escape Miraculously
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Satara, Maharashtra - A 20-year-old tourist from Karad is battling for life after his car skidded off a cliff and plunged 300 feet into a gorge near Satara's popular reverse waterfall on Wednesday.

body.html:
Satara, Maharashtra - A 20-year-old tourist from Karad is battling for life after his car skidded off a cliff and plunged 300 feet into a gorge near Satara's popular reverse waterfall on Wednesday.

Sahil Jadhav was critically injured when the vehicle slipped on wet grass at the notorious Table Point near Sadawaghapur in Patan taluka. The accident occurred whilst his four friends had stepped out to take photographs at the scenic spot.

The group had travelled from Karad to witness the reverse waterfall, which attracts hundreds of tourists during monsoon season. Police sources confirmed that the car's tyres lost grip on the rain-soaked grass, causing Sahil to lose control before the vehicle tumbled into the deep valley.

Police Inspector Avinash Kavathekar, along with students from Kingmaker Academy in Surul, conducted the rescue operation. Sahil was immediately rushed to Sahyadri Hospital in Karad where he remains in critical condition.

The Patan-Sadawaghapur road stretch, particularly the Table Point area, is known for its dangerous gorges on both sides despite being a popular tourist destination.

"Many tourists visit this spot daily. Whilst enjoying the natural beauty, people must exercise extreme caution near Table Point as both sides have deep valleys," police warned in their advisory.

Authorities have urged tourists to prioritise safety over photography, stating that negligence could prove fatal at such risky locations.
